land.text: the south-east of the Hittite Empire: Carchemish and the Syro-Hittite lands

predecessors.note: The page says the states 'arose following the collapse of the Hittite New Kingdom in the 12th century BCE'.

land.text: the Syro-Hittite states, subdued by Assyria in the 8th century BCE; Carchemish conquered by Sargon II in 717

successors.note: Neighbouring Tabal (tabal-kingdom, Cliopatria -900..-701) is a separate row; the Neo-Hittite page lists the Tabalian region among its northern group.

capitals.name: Carchemish (Jerablus)
capitals.note: Seat of the 'Great King' line from Kuzi-Teshub (c. 1175 to 975), then 'a more local city state centered around Carchemish'; the other kingdoms had their own seats (Melid, Tell Tayinat for Palistin, Arpad, Sam'al, Hamath), so the dot is the senior city of the league, not a capital in the strict sense. [Fix 2026-10-19: drawn from -1180, the year the Hittite dossier hands the land over; the page's own 'c. 1175' is five years later.]

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1150 shape (24,444 km2 around Carchemish, Gurgum and the Amuq) taken back to the founding

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (start moved from -1175 to -1180 in the fix pass, to meet the Hittite hand-over): Cliopatria begins in -1150, but the Carchemish page has Kuzi-Teshub and his successors holding the title 'Great King' and ruling a 'mini-empire' from c. 1175 to 975 BC, and Hattusa fell c. 1180 (Hittite dossier). The page gives no extent for those first decades, so the -1150 shape is carried back at confidence 1.

24,444 km2 (89 cells, 35.9–38.5 E, 36.0–38.0 N): Carchemish, the Amuq and the Taurus edge. Neither page gives an area, so the infobox cannot be compared. Carchemish survived the Sea Peoples' attacks and stayed the seat of a Neo-Hittite kingdom (Carchemish page).

25,034 km2, +2.4 percent. The Neo-Hittite page splits the states into a northern group where Hittite rulers stayed (Kammanu, Hilakku, Hiyawa, Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish) and a southern group where Arameans ruled from about 1000 BCE (Palistin, Bit Gabbari, Bit Adini, Bit Bahiani, Pattin, Bit Agusi, Hamath), so the shape mixes Luwian and Aramean kingdoms from this date; the step itself is not explained by either page.

Cliopatria's last shape (25,034 km2, -900..-801) is carried on; the row ends 84 years before the last Neo-Hittite capital falls. The Carchemish page has Sangara (c. 870–848) paying tribute to Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III, then Carchemish largely absent from Assyrian sources until the mid-8th century (apart from Samsi-Adad V, 824–811), and Sargon II conquering it in 717. The shape stands for -900..-801 as drawn and continues as the next keyframe.

correction.text: the Syro-Hittite kingdoms still ruled by their own kings and paying tribute

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -800..-741: the 900 shape continued at confidence 1 as Assyrian tributaries with their own kings. The Neo-Assyrian dossier's -800 shape covers the same cells (it widens west to 34.5 E), so the two overlap until 717: the rendering agent should draw the Neo-Hittite states as Assyrian tributaries (lighter tint) from the first tribute, or accept the overlap. Fix 2026-10-19: the overlap is now explicit as a vassal_start by neo-assyrian-empire at -868 (Carchemish page: Sangara's tribute) to -717.
New keyframe: Tiglath-Pileser III campaigned against Arpad in 743–740 with a lengthy siege, capturing it in 740; its lands became two provinces. The Arpad circle (11 cells of the shape) is cut out.

correction.text: the 900 shape without Arpad and Pattin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in 738 he annexed Pattin (the Amuq, Hatay province) and created the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra; Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwê paid tribute after Arpad. What remains is the Carchemish, Gurgum and Kummuh hull (Hama, kept as a vassal, lies south of the shape).

region.text: Carchemish and the Syro-Hittite lands of south-east Anatolia and north-west Syria

ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: Carchemish under Kuzi-Teshub carries on the Hittite crown after the fall of Hatti. The Carchemish page (reopened 2026-10-19) has Kuzi-Teshub, son of Talmi-Teshub, who 'claimed the title of "Great King" after the fall of Hatti', and dates the polity 'from c. 1175 to 975 BC'; the Hittites page has Hattusa 'burnt to the ground sometime around 1180 BC' and the Hittite dossier hands the land over at -1180 (/ledger/23, /25), so the state starts there, five years before the page's c. 1175 [fix pass]. The Neo-Hittite page: the states 'arose following the collapse of the Hittite New Kingdom in the 12th century BCE', and Hawkins traced a dynastic link between Hittite rulers and the rulers of Melid and Karkamish.

region.text: the Syro-Hittite kingdoms of the -900 shape, of which the page names Carchemish alone as a tributary

ledger.note: c. 868 BC: Carchemish pays tribute to Assyria. Sangara (870-848) 'paid tribute to Kings Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III of Assyria' as 'a tributary probably at some time before 868 BC' (Carchemish page, reopened 2026-10-19); the page names Carchemish alone, and the rest of the -900 hull is the Cliopatria shape that the Neo-Assyrian -800 shape also covers, so the overlap is drawn as a tributary tint. The Neo-Hittite states are the vassal, the Assyrian empire the suzerain; me-02 should mirror it and take these cells out of its -800 gain or mark them vassal (reviewer fix).

740 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Arpad. He campaigned against Arpad over three years (743–740) and a lengthy siege, capturing it in 740; its lands became two provinces. The page names no Neo-Hittite king; Arpad is Aramean (Bit Agusi) on the Neo-Hittite page's southern list.

region.text: Pattin (Unqi), the Amuq plain, with Kullania as its province

ledger.note: 738 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes Pattin. In 738 he annexed Pattin and created the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra; Hama was spared and kept as a vassal. The Hatay province stands for Pattin, which the Neo-Hittite page lists as Pattin/Unqi (Kinalua) among the southern states.

region.text: Carchemish, Gurgum, Kummuh and the rest of the hull after Arpad and Pattin

ledger.note: 717 BC: Sargon II conquers Carchemish. The Carchemish page: Sargon II conquered it in 717 BC in the reign of Pisiri, last ruler of the House of Astiruwa, and the Assyrians set up a provincial capital at Til-Barsip. The Neo-Hittite page says only that Assyria subdued the states in the 8th century BCE; the Tiglath-Pileser III page (third page) dates Arpad 740 and Pattin 738, the Neo-Hittite page gives no conquest dates.
717 BC: the last Neo-Hittite kingdom falls. Carchemish was the 'Great King's' seat for two centuries and the last of the Hatti-line states to be absorbed.

region.text: Carchemish, Gurgum, Kummuh and the rest of the hull after Arpad and Pattin

ledger.note: 717 BC: the tributary status ends with Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish ('conquered by Sargon II in 717 BC in the reign of King Pisiri'); the cells pass to Assyria in the loss below. Arpad (740) and Pattin (738) had left the vassal land earlier.

wars.name: Assyrian tribute demands on Carchemish (Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III)

zones.text: Carchemish on the Euphrates, whose king paid the tribute

wars.outcome: Sangara of Carchemish (c. 870–848) appears as a tributary on the Balawat Bronze Bands, 'probably at some time before 868 BC', and paid tribute to Shalmaneser III; no territory changes.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the start of Shalmaneser III's tribute.

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser III's conquest of Arpad and Pattin
wars.outcome: Arpad captured in 740 after a three-year campaign (743–740) and its lands made two provinces; Pattin annexed in 738 and the provinces of Kullania, Hatarikka and Simirra created; Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwê paid tribute afterwards.
wars.note: The page does not call Arpad Neo-Hittite; the Neo-Hittite page lists it in the Aramean southern group.

wars.name: Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish
wars.outcome: Carchemish conquered in 717 BC during Pisiri's reign; the city becomes Assyrian, with a provincial capital at Til-Barsip.
wars.note: The Carchemish page does not say whether it became a vassal state or a province.

certainty.note: Small kingdoms with no treaty or survey line; the Cliopatria shape is a rough hull around the Syro-Hittite cities, and the southern Aramean kingdoms inside it are not separated.

sources.title: Neo-Hittite states
sources.note: Origin after the collapse of the Hittite New Kingdom, the northern (Hittite-ruled) and southern (Aramean) groups, the capitals; no infobox dates or Assyrian conquest dates.

sources.title: Carchemish
sources.note: Kuzi-Teshub's Great Kings c. 1175–975, Sangara's tribute to Ashurnasirpal II (before 868) and Shalmaneser III, Sargon II's conquest in 717.

sources.title: Tiglath-Pileser III
sources.note: Third page, over this dossier's budget: opened for the Philistia and Phoenicia dossiers and used here for Arpad (740), Pattin (738) and the tribute of Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwê after 740.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'Neo-Hittite states' -1150..-801, 3 shapes, one Seshat polity (tr_neo_hittite_k). The row ends 84 years before Carchemish falls (717) and 54 years after the Great Kings' line ends (975); the dossier starts at -1175 (new keyframe) and ends at -717 (new keyframe -800..-718). A gap-filler should open 'Melid', 'Gurgum', 'Kummuh' and 'Hamath' for the dates of the other states' falls. OVERLAPS: the Neo-Assyrian shape from -800 covers the same cells; Bit Adini (bit-adini, -1000..-856, a 70 km circle at 38.1 E, 36.7 N) and Bit Bahiani (bit-bahiani) are separate dossiers inside or beside this hull; the Tabal Kingdom row (-900..-701) is a neighbour. The Neo-Hittite page's northern group includes the Tabalian region. AREA: no area on either page. PAGE BUDGET: two pages (Neo-Hittite states, Carchemish) plus Tiglath-Pileser III; the Neo-Hittite page gave no dates for any Assyrian conquest and no infobox, and the Carchemish page only the 717 conquest. The Hittites page (Hittite dossier) says Carchemish and Melid became Assyrian vassals under Shalmaneser III (858–823) and were fully absorbed under Sargon II (722–705); it is not cited here. Melid, Gurgum and Kummuh have no dated fall on any page opened. ASSYRIAN VASSALAGE: Carchemish paid tribute from before 868, and Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwê after 740 (Tiglath-Pileser III page): vassal_start events for the Neo-Assyrian dossier, which does not yet have them. COUNTERPARTS WANTED: carchemish/melid/gurgum/kummuh/sam-al/arpad/hamath as separate states if the gap-fillers split the hull. Gazetteer names wanted: Carchemish, Melid (Malatya exists as a place), Til Barsip, Kinalua. FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): start moved from -1175 to -1180 (identity, found event, keyframe -1180, capital and certainty) to meet the Hittite hand-over (hittites /ledger/23, /25); the page's c. 1175 stays in the notes as a disagreement of five years. Added vassal_start/vassal_end by neo-assyrian-empire (-868..-717, Carchemish page) so the -800 overlap with the Neo-Assyrian shape draws as a tributary tint; the page names Carchemish only, the rest of the hull is the Cliopatria shape, and me-02 should mirror it. Not done: dated falls for Melid, Gurgum, Kummuh, Sam'al, Hamath and the post-740 tribute of Gurgum and Kummuh (the Tiglath-Pileser III page is the only source opened; Melid and Gurgum pages not opened in this pass).
